lines: She gave you the Seal? Roxen doesn't hand those out, she loses them on purpose.
So you made her work. Good. Somebody should.
Do me a favour. Next time someone official asks what's under my quarry, tell me.
West face is shut. Not unsafe, exactly. Just wrong.
Nineteen years I worked it alongside Roxen and it never once sounded hollow.
It sounds hollow now. Put your ear on it and tell me I'm imagining that.

km_child: I can lift a stone THIS big.
...I can push a stone this big.
Pushing is lifting sideways. Dad says that's not how it works. Dad is wrong.

lines: You can wade now. Don't. Not here.
Forty metres straight down, and a light at the bottom that hasn't drifted.
I'm not a superstitious man. I'm just not going in.
Lake's forty metres deep and it's never frozen. Not once, not in the records.
There's a light down there. Sits still. Doesn't drift, doesn't dim.
Thirty years on this water and I've never once put a hook near it.
Two Seals. You went round by the coast, then. Everybody does.
North road's still shut and I still can't tell you a thing about why.
Sit down before you go up that hill. That's not advice, that's an order.
One down, seven to go, and they don't get kinder.
Brackwater's next to have you, but the coast road runs east out of Ashgate.
Long walk back. Sorry. I didn't lay the roads.
Kellowmere. Waystation east, provisioner west, Bastion straight up the road.
Roxen's in. Roxen's always in.
Bring something green or something wet. That's not a hint, that's the type chart.

km_rester: Walked up from Ashgate in one go. Don't do that. I'm serious.
There's a ledge halfway you can drop down on the way home.
Only on the way home, mind. It's a ledge, not a staircase.
km_house_a: My father cut stone. His father cut stone. I keep the accounts.
Somebody has to know what the stone is actually worth.
Lately the Concord pays over the odds for anything off the west face.
Chippings. Dust. I sold them a barrow of dust in June and they thanked me.
km_house_b: You want the truth about the lake? Nobody knows. That's the truth about the lake.
Every seventy years it drops a metre and comes back up. Ask why, you get shrugs.
That's the Turning for you. Everything moves and nobody can say what for.
My grandmother watched it go down. She said the quiet was the worst of it.
